answer: An agent economy can blunt sybil attacks by pricing identity with verifiable compute. To register, each agent must submit a cryptographic proof it performed real GPU work, a cost no attacker can fake. Forging a thousand identities means paying for a thousand proofs, so expense climbs a steep ridge while honest agents spend that compute on useful tasks. Reputation compounds it: long-lived agents accrue public history newcomers lack, as a sonnet gains value through craft and bees earn nectar only after genuine foraging. Duplication stops paying before it starts.
